eligibility.aid_cap: No sport-specific scholarship limit; aid may go to any rostered athlete up to the roster limit.
eligibility.gpa_rule: 16 core courses; 10 of 16 (7 in English/math/science) before the 7th semester (10/7); minimum 2.3 core GPA; final transcript with proof of graduation.
eligibility.caveat: Aid cannot be revoked for roster management, performance or injury unless the athlete chooses to transfer. Designated Student-Athletes do not count toward the roster limit. A conference may set a lower roster limit, but not below the sport's 2024-25 D1 scholarship limit.

rules_moving.title: D1 age-based eligibility
rules_moving.text: Approved by the D1 Cabinet 2026-06-23; NCAA noted the changes were not final until the meeting concluded Wednesday 2026-06-24. The 2026-07-31 deadline for waiver requests under the old rules is past. Up to five years if the athlete enrolls no later than the academic year after the 19th birthday; fully effective for fall 2027 first-time enrollees; fall 2026 enrollees get the better of old or new rules.

source.label: NCAA: Division I adopts age-based eligibility model

rules_moving.title: Two-year transfer GPA (D1)
rules_moving.text: The 2025-26 NCAA Two-Year Transfer Guide still reads 2.5 for D1 (and 2.2 for D2). A change to 2.0 is unconfirmed by any NCAA primary document.

bucket3.why_unpublished: No football program and no baseball program with a published numeric cutoff was found in the W7 pass. Absence is 'not found', not proof none exist. Track programs publish marks because the event is measured by a clock; football and baseball fit depends on position, scheme, roster need and film.
evaluated: Verified camp or showcase measurables, dated and tied to a named event (40-yard time, height/weight, pitch velocity, exit velocity, pop time)
Position depth and roster need in the class you would sign in
Academics against that school's own admissions bar
Character, coachability and what your own coaches say
bucket3.aggregator_note: Third-party tables (NCSA, NextCommit, Go Big, Premier Athletes, Scorability) are a vendor's composite or estimate, not NCAA standards and not any program's statement. They disagree with each other: the D1 pitcher floor is '84 mph consistently' (NCSA, Go Big) vs '88 to 92 mid-major' (NextCommit) vs 'average fastball 85 / top 88.4 D1 mid-major' (Premier Athletes). Two guides state outright that no official chart exists.
bucket3.action: Ask the coach what they evaluate. A number that fits one program may not describe another.

ratio_source.label: NCAA Estimated Probability of Competing Beyond High School (2024-25 data, updated March 2026)

ratio_method: A ratio of two headcounts in the same year: NCAA participants in 2024-25 divided by high school participants in 2024-25.
High school counts exclude club teams.
NCAA counts exclude NAIA and NJCAA, so the all-levels figure for a family considering every level is understated.
Counts every rostered athlete (walk-ons, transfers, international athletes), not only recruited high school seniors.
Not an individual athlete's probability and says nothing about any athlete's measurables.
